Title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in UrlField due to lack of protocol validation on href
Analysis:
The `UrlField` component is used to display URLs from records in react-admin. It fetches the URL value from the record context using `const value = get(record, source);` and passes it directly to the `href` attribute of the `@mui/material/Link` component without any sanitization or validation of the protocol/scheme.

If a malicious user or data source supplies a URL starting with a `javascript:` scheme (e.g., `javascript:alert(document.cookie)`), clicking the link will execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the user's session, leading to Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Create a record with a URL field set to:
```
javascript:alert(document.domain)
```
When this record is displayed in a Datagrid or Show view utilizing `UrlField` (e.g., `<UrlField source="website" />`), a user clicking the link will trigger the XSS payload.

Title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in FileField due to unsanitized href values
Analysis:
The `FileField` component is used to render links to downloadable files or documents. It retrieves the URL/source values from the record (either directly via `sourceValue` or nested within an array for multiple files) and assigns them to the `href` attribute of the Material UI `<Link>` component without sanitization or scheme validation.

If a file path or URL within a record is supplied with a `javascript:` URL scheme (e.g., `javascript:alert(1)`), clicking the file link executes arbitrary JS in the user's browser context, resulting in Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A record contains file data where the source or URL field is:
```json
{
  "id": 123,
  "file_url": "javascript:alert('XSS')",
  "title": "Malicious Document"
}
```
When `<FileField source="file_url" title="title" />` renders this record, the resulting anchor element will have `href="javascript:alert('XSS')"`, which triggers on click.
